user_problem: Which package is cheaper per gram / per ounce / per item?
inputs: 2-3 products; for each: price; quantity; unit (g; kg; ml; l; oz; lb; count)
outputs: Normalised unit price per common base unit; cheapest flag; percentage saving; total cost at equal quantity
formula: unit_price = price / quantity_in_base_unit; compare only after converting to a shared base unit (g or ml or count)
edge_cases: Mixed units (lb vs kg); multi-buy promotions (3 for 2); count vs weight products; zero or blank quantity; display rounding; single-currency assumption must be stated
usefulness_beyond_competitor: Multi-item side-by-side normalisation with saving percentage; omnicalculator's three pages are single-item converters
required_content_and_example: Worked example (500g at 4.00 vs 750g at 5.25 => 0.80 vs 0.70 per 100g); shortenflation note; 4 FAQs; state the rounding rule
acceptance_tests: 500g@4.00 vs 750g@5.25 -> 0.80 vs 0.70 per 100g and correct winner; lb to g conversion; blank row ignored; zero quantity blocked; 3-item ranking stable

existing_equivalent_or_overlap: /markup-margin-calculator covers margin and markup only; no break-even tool
user_problem: How many units must I sell to cover fixed costs?
inputs: Fixed costs; unit selling price; variable cost per unit
outputs: Break-even units; break-even revenue; contribution margin per unit and %; margin of safety
formula: BEP_units = fixed_costs / (price - variable_cost); BEP_revenue = BEP_units x price
edge_cases: Price <= variable cost => no break-even (must show an explicit error; never Infinity); zero fixed costs; stepped or tiered pricing; tax ignored statement
usefulness_beyond_competitor: Profit-versus-units chart (ECharts already in the repo) plus margin of safety; competitors are bare forms
required_content_and_example: Worked example (fixed 10000; price 25; variable 15 => 1000 units; revenue 25000); explain contribution margin; 4 FAQs
implementation_complexity: config for outputs OR custom for chart
acceptance_tests: 10000/25/15 -> 1000 units and 25000 revenue; price == variable cost -> error state not Infinity; zero fixed costs -> 0 units; chart renders
notes: Config build is possible; chart makes it a custom component.

existing_equivalent_or_overlap: /credit-card-payoff-calculator handles ONE debt via the log formula; /debt-consolidation-calculator and /loan-payment-calculator are single-loan; no multi-debt planner
user_problem: I have several debts; which do I clear first and when am I debt-free?
inputs: 2-10 debts: balance; APR; minimum payment. Extra monthly budget. Strategy: snowball (lowest balance) or avalanche (highest APR)
outputs: Payoff order; months to debt-free; total interest paid; interest saved vs minimums-only; side-by-side strategy comparison; payoff timeline
formula: Per month: interest = balance x APR/12/100; pay every minimum; apply the remainder to the target debt; repeat until all balances are zero
edge_cases: Payment below total interest => balances grow (must detect and warn; cap iterations at e.g. 1200 months); APR 0; equal balances tie-break; minimum below interest; negative/nonsense input
usefulness_beyond_competitor: Snowball vs avalanche side-by-side plus interest-saved and a timeline chart; no catalogued competitor combines multi-debt ordering with strategy comparison in one view
required_content_and_example: Worked example with two debts (1000 at 20%; 2000 at 5%; extra 100) showing avalanche vs snowball difference; explain the strategies; 5 FAQs; state the simulation assumptions
acceptance_tests: Two-debt case clears the 20% APR debt first under avalanche; total interest is finite; both strategies produce different totals; non-amortising case raises a warning and terminates; 10-debt case completes under the cap
notes: Highest-value item in the batch. Simulation must terminate by construction.

existing_equivalent_or_overlap: /loan-payment-calculator is generic (amount; rate; years) and ALREADY carries the keywords auto loan and car loan - direct cannibalisation risk
user_problem: What will my monthly car payment be including tax; fees and trade-in?
inputs: Vehicle price; down payment; trade-in value; sales tax %; fees; APR; term in months
outputs: Amount financed; monthly payment; total interest; total cost of the vehicle
formula: financed = price - down - trade-in + tax_on(price - trade-in) + fees; M = financed x r x (1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1)
edge_cases: Zero APR => r = 0 causes division by zero in the standard formula (must fall back to financed/n); trade-in greater than price (negative equity); fees financed vs paid upfront; tax base differs by jurisdiction (must be an input; not hard-coded)
usefulness_beyond_competitor: Models tax; trade-in and fees which the generic loan tool cannot; but the core maths duplicates it - value depends on those extra inputs
required_content_and_example: Worked example (25000 price; 3000 down; 1000 trade-in; 7% tax; 500 fees; 6% APR; 60 months) with each step shown; state the tax-base assumption; 4 FAQs
acceptance_tests: Financed amount matches hand calculation; zero APR returns financed/n without NaN; negative trade-in handled; payment matches loan-payment-calculator when tax/fees/trade-in are zero
notes: CONDITION: if built; remove auto loan and car loan from loan-payment-calculator keywords in the same change; otherwise the two pages compete. Alternative: extend loan-payment-calculator with a vehicle mode instead of a new route.

existing_equivalent_or_overlap: /fraction-to-percent-calculator converts one fraction to a percentage; no arithmetic; /ratio-proportion-calculator is different
user_problem: Add; subtract; multiply or divide fractions and simplify the result
inputs: Two fractions a/b and c/d; operator; optional mixed numbers
outputs: Result as a simplified fraction; mixed number; decimal; step-by-step working
formula: a/b +/- c/d = (ad +/- cb)/bd; a/b x c/d = ac/bd; a/b / c/d = ad/bc; simplify by gcd(|numerator|; |denominator|)
edge_cases: Zero denominator (must block with a message); negative denominators (normalise the sign); mixed numbers converted to improper; overflow on large numerators (use integer-safe maths); gcd(0; n) = n
usefulness_beyond_competitor: Step-by-step working and mixed-number support; calculator.net publishes 12 fraction pages but shows no working
required_content_and_example: Worked example (1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6) with the common-denominator step shown; explain simplification; 4 FAQs
notes: Steps are the differentiator; a config entry cannot render working.

existing_equivalent_or_overlap: /work-hours-calculator is one day only (start; end; break; 24-hour integers); /weekly-hours-calculator and /decimal-hours-calculator are narrower
user_problem: Total hours and pay for a whole week including overtime
inputs: Per day (7 rows): clock in; clock out; unpaid break. Hourly rate; overtime threshold and multiplier
outputs: Daily hours; weekly total; regular vs overtime split; gross pay
formula: daily = out - in - break; weekly = sum(daily); overtime = max(0; weekly - threshold) x multiplier
edge_cases: Overnight shifts (out < in => add 24h; work-hours-calculator currently yields a negative figure); multiple shifts per day; paid vs unpaid breaks; daily vs weekly overtime rules; minute rounding; empty days
usefulness_beyond_competitor: A multi-day grid with an overtime split and pay total; the existing tool cannot represent a week
required_content_and_example: Worked example (5 x 8h at 20/hour = 800; 45h with a 40h threshold at 1.5 = 950); explain overtime rules by jurisdiction; 4 FAQs
acceptance_tests: 5 days x 8h at 20 => 40h and 800; 45h with threshold 40 and x1.5 => 950; 22:00-06:00 => 8h not negative; empty day ignored; break subtracted
notes: The overnight underflow is a confirmed defect in the existing work-hours tool and an acceptance test here.

user_problem: How many shingles / bundles / squares do I need and what will it cost?
inputs: Roof area OR footprint plus pitch; waste %; bundle coverage (default 3 per square); optional price per bundle
outputs: Squares; bundles; underlayment rolls; nails; total cost
formula: squares = area / 100; pitch_multiplier = sqrt(1 + (rise/12)^2); area = footprint x multiplier; bundles = ceil(squares x 3 x (1 + waste))
edge_cases: Pitch 0 (flat membrane; not shingles); multiple roof planes summed; package rounding up; waste by roof complexity; metric vs imperial squares; footprint vs actual-area confusion must be explicit
usefulness_beyond_competitor: Pitch-multiplier conversion from a footprint plus waste and cost; the catalogue has no roofing capability while five competitors do
required_content_and_example: Worked example (2000 sq ft footprint; 6/12 pitch => multiplier 1.118 => 2236 sq ft => 22.36 squares => 68 bundles; +10% waste => 75 bundles); pitch table; 4 FAQs
implementation_complexity: config if area is given; custom if pitch-based
acceptance_tests: 6/12 multiplier ~= 1.118; 2000 sq ft -> ~22.4 squares; bundles round UP; +10% waste applied before rounding; pitch 0 switches to a flat-roof note rather than shingles
notes: Seed list explicitly names roofing; closest parity gap in construction.
